newsitem.title: USA: Compaq says set to exceed workstation goal. [CORRECTED 21:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Compaq says set to exceed workstation goal. [CORRECTED 21:05 GMT]

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp Senior Vice President John Rose said the company expects to exceed its goal of shipping 100,000 professional workstations within 12 to 15 (corrects from 12 to 18) months of its entry into the fiercely competitive market.

Compaq entered the market for workstations, used by engineers and designers for number-crunching graphics and development projects, just a little more than seven months ago and introduced two new models here Monday.

Rose, group general manager of Compaq's Enterprise Computing Group, said after a news briefing here that the company's higher-end computing business accounted for 29 percent of Compaq's revenues in the first quarter, when it was comprised almost entirely of Windows NT servers, with initial workstation sales.

Compaq's goal is for its enterprise business -- which represents its higher-end server and workstation operations -- to become 50 percent of revenues by the year 2000, Rose told Reuters in an interview.
"The enterprise is clearly strategic," Rose said. ((sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau 415 846 5400))
